# About this edition {.unnumbered}

This manual describes **skyscapeR 2.0**, development build 2.0.9016. It explains how a measured bearing becomes an astronomical result, which assumptions enter the calculation and how closely the result agrees with independent evidence.

## Finding a method

Use the [function index](function-index.qmd) for arguments, defaults and methodological notes. The [methods guide](contents-plan.qmd) groups calculations by research question. The [vignette guide](vignette-guide.qmd) follows the worked analysis from field observations to interpretation.

## Finding the evidence

The [study register](study-register.qmd) distinguishes numerical checks, field comparisons and empirical calibration. For site horizons, start with [surveyed altitude residuals](h01-field-validation.qmd) and [matched skyline comparisons](h02-skyline-comparison.qmd). For visibility, see the [Milky Way and diffuse brightness model](sky-rendering.qmd) and [heliacal-rising dates](heliacal-rising.qmd). For statistical inference, see [uniform bearings](s01-uniform-orientation.qmd), [specified null models](s02-specified-models.qmd) and [Monte Carlo scores](s03-scoring-checks.qmd).
